images.title: Constructing a 60° angle
images.purpose: Show two equal arcs making an equilateral triangle ABC, and the 60° angle at A.
images.composition: A ray from A going right along the bottom; two arcs above it meeting at C.
exact_structure: A dark ray from A to the right, labelled A at its start and X at its end.
A grey (#6B7280) arc centred at A cutting AX at B, labelled B, and rising above the ray.
A grey (#6B7280) arc centred at B, of the same radius, crossing the first arc at C, labelled C.
Thin dashed amber (#E69F00) segments AC and BC; AB, AC and BC each carry one tick mark.
A teal (#0072B2) ray from A through C, and a small reddish purple (#CC79A7) angle arc at A labelled 60°.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: AB = AC = BC, so triangle ABC is equilateral and the angle at A is 60°.

image_decisions.why: The equilateral triangle hidden in the construction explains why the angle is 60°.
